rubric_answers.question: subject placement (thirds / centre) is deliberate
rubric_answers.answer: Pip is centred or slightly left in the character shots (S01, S02, S05). Evidence windows are centred. Fine.

rubric_answers.question: headroom and look-room are comfortable
rubric_answers.answer: S05 has good headroom after the camera was moved closer. S01 and S02 crop the feet and show the antenna; the face is clear in all three.

rubric_answers.question: nothing important is covered by captions, overlays or platform buttons
rubric_answers.answer: In the first S05 render the left hand covered the visor rim (fixed: pose changed and re-rendered, checked on a 405x720 still). Captions sit on Pip's torso in S01 and S02, not on the face.

rubric_answers.question: foreground/background separation (focus, light, colour)
rubric_answers.answer: Pip separates well from the cream wall (orange body, dark visor). On the end card the headline sits on a blurred workshop wall with only moderate contrast.

findings.problem: End card: the top 40 percent of the frame is empty teal, the CTA pill is small, and the not-yet-spoken caption word is grey on a busy wall.
findings.evidence: S10.png: headline at y 840-930, pill at y 1010-1100, top 800 px empty; caption 'you the' with 'the' in low-contrast grey at y 1490
findings.expected: a call to action large enough to read at arm length, content balanced in the frame
findings.fix: raise the headline and enlarge the pill (EndCard props) or accept as a calm ending; decide at the contact-sheet review
